name: Maximum Independent Set
problem_statement: Find an independent vertex set of maximum cardinality in a simple undirected graph.

normalization: Preserve external vertex identities and isolated vertices.
Reject self-loops and collapse parallel edges only under the declared aggregation rule.

problem_inputs.name: mode
problem_inputs.description: Exact optimization or an explicitly heuristic feasible solution.

problem_inputs.name: time_limit_seconds
problem_inputs.description: Positive runtime budget; expiry must report incomplete optimization.

required_outputs.name: optimality_proven
required_outputs.description: True only if a valid exact proof or exhausted search establishes optimality.

required_outputs.name: termination_reason
required_outputs.description: Convergence, exhausted search, timeout, or other explicit reason.

solution_semantics.objective: Find an independent vertex set of maximum cardinality in a simple undirected graph.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mathematical objective; implementations must declare approximation and termination status.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each external vertex ID occurs once; output multiplicities follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering among equally valid solutions is required.

validation_rules: Check every returned ID and every edge for independent-set feasibility.
On small graphs compare cardinality with exhaustive search.
A maximal independent set is not necessarily maximum; local maximality does not prove optimality.
Heuristic and learned methods must set optimality_proven=false absent a separate proof.
edge_cases: The empty graph has the empty optimum.
All isolated vertices belong to every maximum-cardinality solution.
Disconnected components can be solved independently.
